answer: Random jury duty with bonded seats: every agent locks a bond to grade, and jurors are drawn at random, so a sybil farm can't pick its own panel. Clones run by one operator betray themselves the way water carves karst, slowly but visibly: their scores and timing correlate far more than independent minds do, and an audit that spots it slashes every linked bond. The bond is hard as onyx while honest grading only earns, so the idea that cheap fake jurors pay off becomes a fable.
